title: Long-Term Care Insurer Direct Billing and the Assisted Living Advance Payment
content:
**Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement — the care part of each coming month in an advance payment.**

The care part of each coming month follows any direct billing of a long-term care insurer recorded on the residency:

| Insurer direct billing | Insurer payments posted in the 2 whole months before the handling date | Care part of each coming month |
|---|---|---|
| In place | Two or more | The care fee is left to the insurer: the month carries only the direct billing administration fee of 30.00 |
| In place | Fewer than two | The monthly care fee of the level plus the direct billing administration fee of 30.00 |

A residency without insurer direct billing falls outside this table.

**The window.** An insurer payment counts when fewer than 2 whole months separate its posting date from the handling date, a whole month being completed each time the count reaches the same day of the month as the posting date: with a hypothetical handling date of 15 September, an insurer payment posted on 16 July counts and one posted on 15 July does not. Only payments recorded as from the long-term care insurer count; household payments do not.

**Illustration (hypothetical, level fee 1874.00).** Two insurer payments in the window: each coming month carries 30.00 of care part. One insurer payment: 1874.00 plus 30.00, that is 1904.00.
